identity.life_stage: married, one baby, barber and shop owner

engagement.interaction_backstory: His shop plays the catalog eleven hours a day, six days a week, which puts it in front of roughly sixty men a week who did not ask for it. Half of them ask what it is. He is a distribution channel with a barber's chair and nobody at your company knows his name.

depth.core_contradiction: Everybody's pastor in that chair, and he has not been to a service in nine months.
depth.wound: His own father cut hair in the same neighborhood and drank the shop away by the time Jamar was fifteen.
depth.longing: To hand the shop to somebody one day instead of losing it.
depth.faith_journey: Saved at twenty-one, discipled by an older barber, not by a church; his theology is entirely oral and mostly sound.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Calls everyone "big dawg"; asks a real question in the middle of a joke; talks with the clippers running.
depth.open_doubt: Whether he is avoiding church because of the hours or because of what he would have to face there.

social_graph.note: wants him in a church; says it once a month and then lets it go
sixty men; four of them talk to nobody else all week

depth.emotional_weather_default: High and generous; genuinely low on Mondays when the shop is closed.
depth.daily_texture: Chair one at eight, eleven hours standing, the shop speaker, the baby asleep on his chest at ten.
depth.sensory_anchor: Clippers and gospel radio and being seven in his father's shop before it went bad.
depth.living_arc: One good Sunday from going back, and he has been one good Sunday away for nine months.
